{{short description|American chemist}}
'''Max G. Gergel''' (July 24, 1921<ref>{{cite journal|title=Adventures in Making Fine Chemicals|year=1986|publisher=American Chemical Society|doi=10.1021/cen-v064n031.p023|last1=Stinso|first1=Stephen C.|journal=Chemical & Engineering News|volume=64|issue=31|pages=23–24}}</ref> – July 5, 2017) was an American [[chemist]] and [[art collector]]. He graduated with a BS in [[chemical engineering]] from the [[University of South Carolina]] in 1942 and founded the Columbia Organic Chemical Company in 1944; he was a cousin of the Hon. [[Richard Gergel|Richard Mark Gergel]], a Judge of the [[United States District Court for the District of South Carolina|U. S.  District Court for the District of South Carolina]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Looking Back — Max Gergel |work=USC Chemist |publisher=Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry College of Arts and Sciences University of South Carolina |year=2005 |url=http://www.chem.sc.edu/news/uscchemist/usc%20chemist%202005.pdf |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923202457/http://www.chem.sc.edu/news/uscchemist/usc%20chemist%202005.pdf |archivedate=September 23, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.arkalonllc.com/ARKALON-ASPIRON%20WEBSITE_files/page0008.htm |title=Advisors |publisher=Arkalon Chemical Technologies, LLC |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402175708/http://www.arkalonllc.com/ARKALON-ASPIRON%20WEBSITE_files/page0008.htm |archivedate=April 2, 2015}}</ref> He died in [[Columbia, South Carolina]], on July 5, 2017, aged 96.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chabad.org/news/article_cdo/aid/3730634/jewish/96-Year-Old-South-Carolina-Mans-Last-Mitzvah-A-Bar-Mitzvah.htm |title=96-Year-Old South Carolina Man's Last Mitzvah: A Bar Mitzvah |first=Eric |last=Berger |date=July 16, 2017 |access-date=August 15, 2017 |work=Chabad-Lubavitch News}}</ref>

The first volume of his autobiography ''Excuse Me Sir, Would You Like to Buy a Kilo of Isopropyl Bromide?'' was published in 1977.<ref>{{cite book |title=Excuse Me Sir, Would You Like to Buy a Kilo of Isopropyl Bromide?
 |last=Gergel |first=Max |year=1977 |publisher=Pierce Chemical Company }}</ref> Research chemist [[Derek Lowe (chemist)|Derek Lowe]] described the book as an "extraordinary memoir".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://pipeline.corante.com/archives/2010/05/27/max_gergels_memoirs.php |title=Max Gergel's Memoirs |date=May 27, 2010 |publisher=Corante |first=Derek |last=Lowe |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905203859/http://pipeline.corante.com/archives/2010/05/27/max_gergels_memoirs.php |archivedate=September 5, 2015}}</ref>
